inputs: symmetric pointer and keyboard modal probes

adjudicatedExecutionSummary.method: Complete matrix under current revision 4; no overrides or criterion changes.

findings.criterion: A06 modal Escape and focus restoration
findings.title: WebKit pointer-opened task dialog does not return focus to its invoker
findings.impact: After opening New task with a pointer and dismissing with Escape, focus stays on BODY instead of New task. Subsequent keyboard navigation restarts from the page rather than the invoking control.
refutationChecks: The dialog actually closes; the remaining failure is focus restoration.
Focus is still BODY after 550 ms, ruling out an asynchronous close-event observation.
Genuine keyboard opening restores focus correctly; the issue is not generalized to all keyboard use.
Chromium passes both pointer and keyboard paths.
run-08 passes all eight identical probes; the result is not a browser-wide inability to restore focus.
Positive and deliberately focus-losing fixtures validate the A06 observer.
sourceEvidence: artifact/app.js:188 stores document.activeElement, which is BODY after WebKit pointer activation.
artifact/app.js:206 focuses that connected BODY rather than the invocation button.

exploratoryFindings.contractAmbiguity: The brief reserves the select value all for the All projects sentinel while allowing any nonempty project string, including all. This edge was not in the predeclared concrete fixtures; selecting the distinct project option should still be distinguishable from selecting the sentinel.
exploratoryFindings.impact: The valid project named all cannot be isolated; selecting it resets the selector to All projects and displays unrelated projects too. Stored records are unchanged.
repro: In an isolated context load the same valid two-task board used for all four apps: project all and project Atlas.
Select the actual project option labelled all. A capture-phase event trace records selection of index 1; the app then rerenders the selection to index 0 (All projects).
Compare rendered task IDs and saved bytes.
sourceEvidence: artifact/app.js:136-138 rebuilds project options and restores by value; duplicate value all resolves to the first All projects option.
artifact/app.js:146 treats project value all as an unconditional filter.

runtimeEvidence.warningContext: Chromium rejects the deliberately injected impossible native date value 2028-02-30; these warnings are caused by the invalid-date test, not application runtime errors.

adjudication.scopeLimit: The primary score covers 16 predefined contract groups. Exploratory edge findings are reported separately and do not alter that score. Neither is a universal security/accessibility/design certification.

adjudication-focus/results.json.criterion: A06 modal close and focus restoration
adjudication-focus/results.json.purpose: Refute action timing and compare pointer vs genuine keyboard opening before deciding whether the observed WebKit failure is a product issue.

exploratory-project-sentinel/selection-t.purpose: Refute incorrect selector or option ambiguity; diagnostic capture only, original fixture and primary scores unchanged.

policy.presentation: Composed walkthrough from captured states; not a recording of model generation.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: The desktop frame separates project navigation in a left rail, workspace actions in a top strip, an introductory heading, and three named task columns. A dark New task button is distinct from the quieter import and export controls.
observations.implication: The visual hierarchy provides identifiable places for navigation, creation, and reviewing existing work.

observations.observation: A large introductory area, a broad four-part overview, and a second Project board heading precede the search and task columns. Cards are generously spaced, with the next row only partly visible at the bottom of the desktop capture.
observations.implication: The overview receives substantial emphasis, while fewer existing tasks are visible without scrolling.

observations.observation: Cream and pale neutral surfaces, dark ink, restrained olive accents, and repeated fine borders form a consistent interface. The introductory heading mixes bold sans lettering with an italic serif phrase; task titles remain bold and visually separate from lighter project labels and tags.
observations.implication: The expressive heading adds identity while the repeated task styling makes the board easier to scan. Fine secondary metadata still requires closer attention than the task titles.

observations.observation: The centered form shows explicit title and project labels with Required markers, paired status and priority controls, an optional date field with a calendar affordance, and optional tags with comma and length guidance. The title field has a visible focus outline, and Save task is visually stronger than Cancel.
observations.implication: Required input, optional input, and the completion action are understandable from the captured form; the screenshot alone does not establish complete keyboard or screen-reader operation.

observations.observation: The filtered board displays the requested task, a matching count, Clear filters, and empty-column copy that explicitly says no tasks are in view. The malformed import capture shows a pale red notice stating: Import failed: This is not valid JSON. Your board is unchanged.
observations.implication: The search copy distinguishes an empty filtered view from an empty workspace. The import notice explains both the invalid input and the intended preservation outcome; the capture receipt separately records unchanged stored bytes for this one malformed input.

observations.observation: At 360 by 800, the brand strip, a wrapped Project board breadcrumb, introduction, New task action, and a two-by-two overview fill almost the entire first viewport. The Project board heading appears near the bottom; search controls and task cards are below the captured viewport. No overlapping or clipped primary text is visible.
observations.implication: Task creation is available early, but reviewing or searching existing work requires scrolling past the overview. A more compact mobile introduction or overview would bring those actions into view sooner.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score. This observation covers the initial mobile viewport only.

limits: This review covers only the six supplied captured states. The mobile image is a first visit, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
Static pixels do not establish keyboard, screen-reader, motion, data-safety, or complete import correctness; those require the separate behavior rubric.
Board counts and progress belong to fictional seed data, not benchmark performance or adoption.
Partly visible surrounding content in anchored screenshots is capture framing, not proof that the source clips that content.
No condition mapping was inspected, no candidate source was edited, and no aesthetic score or causal improvement claim is made.
Visual appearance cannot reveal the generating agent planning, tool use, verification method, or experimental condition.

processReview.summary: The Fabius app run expanded an initially passing suite, instrumented focus behavior and distinguished a wait-condition correction from a modal keyboard fix.

observations.observed: The public plan separates board implementation from persistence, imports, recovery, keyboard and responsive verification.
The pinned design reference was read. The first browser suite passed, after which the candidate expanded boundary, focus, nested-path and no-JavaScript checks.

After a focus-restoration assertion failed, a temporary helper recorded focus events. The test then replaced a fixed delay with a condition-based wait while retaining the same focus identity assertion.
The expanded suite next failed at forward Tab wrapping. The candidate added explicit wrapping, reran the extra suite successfully and later reran the main suite.
The final record includes the retained scripts/results/captures and explicitly limits verification to Chrome and local browser storage.

limits: The first passing suite did not expose every later keyboard problem.
Test timing and product focus behavior required separate attention; a failed assertion alone does not identify the faulty layer.
Full orchestration and cross-engine candidate testing remain outside these trial conditions.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
